nodes.label: GLUE: how it works now (SYSTEM.md)
nodes.rationale: The one place that says how GLUE works today; the ADRs say why. It must stay true in the same commit as any change.

nodes.label: GLUE folder
nodes.rationale: The user's data as JSON files, no database. Lowercase mco names are real file and setting names and stay, because data depends on them.

nodes.label: GLUE Home
nodes.rationale: Tauri tray app on the user's computer. When it runs it is the library's engine and the website on that computer is its screen; the page starts none of the library's work.

nodes.label: GLUE Cloud
nodes.rationale: Optional account on a Cloudflare Worker (D1, a Durable Object for signalling). Holds the account's collections, profiles and devices, never music.

nodes.label: Track (a song)
nodes.rationale: Status is linked, missing or unlinked; rootId and relPath place it in a music folder; importPath, fileKey for copies, and sources are the DJ libraries it came from.

nodes.label: Music folder away, not gone
nodes.rationale: A network folder not connected or a drive not plugged in: its songs are not marked missing, analysed, rescanned or written into. They wait for it.

nodes.label: Removing a music folder
nodes.rationale: Removes this computer's songs in it; songs left with no file are offered once, with a backup first.

nodes.label: Songs with no file
nodes.rationale: Matched to the library's songs on the No file linked page with a certainty each, then linked in bulk: the song takes their playlists and the record's path, so a new read keeps them linked.

nodes.label: Profiles (artist aliases)
nodes.rationale: A profile is an artist alias. Signed in, the account keeps the union of every device's profiles; a deleted profile is final; each device keeps its own choice. One library per GLUE folder.

nodes.label: Shared collection
nodes.rationale: Signed in with cloud sync on, each collection is the account's, one copy in GLUE Cloud. A song has a copy per computer; the same file on two computers is one song with a copy on each.

nodes.label: Shared sync
nodes.rationale: GLUE Cloud keeps a snapshot and a log of changes; only files marked changed are looked at (every file every 30 minutes); merge per field; clashes wait in a box; a computer never clashes with itself.

nodes.label: One id per computer
nodes.rationale: GLUE Home learns the computer's account device id; only the computer's GLUE folder writes its parts; nothing is written under an unknown or stand-in id.

nodes.label: Local link to GLUE Home
nodes.rationale: 127.0.0.1 ports 47400-47409. /connect hands the link's token to the live website's origin, so any browser on the computer gets it; every route but /hello and /connect needs the token.

nodes.label: GLUE Home's engine in Rust
nodes.rationale: One store per collection written straight to disk; the analysis queue; the service (status, timers, backups, updates) in the same engine. Stopped, it answers only GLUE Home's own windows.

nodes.label: Library store in Rust
nodes.rationale: CollectionStore ported line for line with JavaScript's JSON rules, held byte for byte to the TypeScript by tests/golden/store.

nodes.label: CollectionStore
nodes.rationale: One per open collection; loads the files and keeps maps; writes only the files that changed, marked per shard and debounced; atomic writes through a swap file.

nodes.label: DJ libraries in GLUE Home
nodes.rationale: Rekordbox XML, Traktor NML, Apple XML, Serato, Engine DJ's m.db and M3U are read and brought in by Rust, held byte for byte to the website's; the engine follows each library every 5 s.

nodes.label: DJ apps synced both ways
nodes.rationale: Opt-in per library, backup first, app closed; cues, loops and grids merged three ways per slot; Engine DJ first.

nodes.label: The main DJ library
nodes.rationale: One per computer. A song's grid and cues are GLUE's own, else the main library's; the two-way sync is with it.

nodes.label: No writes into Engine DJ
nodes.rationale: Off unless engineWrites is set: after Engine DJ 5.3 rebuilt its Collection and the sync deleted the user's playlists. Reading and following stay on.

nodes.label: GLUE's playlists as a rekordbox XML
nodes.rationale: The lists kept in Engine DJ, with cues and grids, written on this computer as a rekordbox XML that Engine DJ reads as its rekordbox library. GLUE writes none of Engine DJ's files.

nodes.label: GLUE's own Engine DJ library on a drive
nodes.rationale: Shown to Engine DJ as a drive (Windows subst). Engine DJ 5.3 merges each drive's library with its Collection when it starts, so GLUE's lists arrive by themselves. Written only while Engine DJ is closed, after a backup, and only under the GLUE folder.

nodes.label: Analysis pipeline (songs at a time)
nodes.rationale: One pipeline inside songs at a time: songs asked for now, new songs' tags, the library's songs, then thumbnails for other devices. Passing failures are retried and never stored; after the third try the song is saved as failed, with why.

nodes.label: Sound profile
nodes.rationale: Loudness, onsets, timbre and loudness over time per song, from the mono mix; ANALYSIS_VERSION 4 analyses every song once more. Native engine held to the TypeScript by goldens.

nodes.label: Energy 1-10
nodes.rationale: Relative to the collection: rank in loudness (0.45), onsets (0.3), highs (0.15) and BPM (0.1); Mixed In Key's Energy N wins. An absolute energy would put a one-genre collection at one level.

nodes.label: Playlist builder
nodes.rationale: A flow of energy per slot, the songs to start from placed by role, a score, and a beam search. Replaced the greedy fill of ADR 0029; the form is kept on List.auto.

nodes.label: Beam search
nodes.rationale: Eight partial sets kept; deterministic from the seed; Surprise me draws among each set's best few.

nodes.label: Quality verdicts
nodes.rationale: Speklone's forensics. A hi-res file is judged by what reaches past 24 kHz above digital silence; a steep top end with content above and few drop-outs is lossless. A rule change re-judges stored details, never the file.

nodes.label: Duplicates
nodes.rationale: Only the best copy is shown and used; the user can mark a copy as not a duplicate or mark duplicates; the optional main music folder breaks ties after lossless; GLUE Home makes the groups.

nodes.label: Streaming to other devices over WebRTC
nodes.rationale: Signalled through GLUE Cloud; songs play as they arrive; a song's start timing goes to the console only; a room silent for 75 s after a pong is reopened.

nodes.label: Sessions with other devices
nodes.rationale: One per device's tab with each of the account's other GLUE Homes, at most 5 (refused when full). This computer's own GLUE Home never gets one.

nodes.label: What the user asks for goes first
nodes.rationale: Background loads from GLUE Home are gated (3 at a time) and GLUE Home starts no new analysis beyond 2 while a song plays; the running reads wait.

nodes.label: Overviews and covers for rows on screen
nodes.rationale: Newest request first; a row that scrolls away drops its request; from another computer, asked until answered.

nodes.label: The tab in Home mode
nodes.rationale: With GLUE Home running the tab starts none of the library's work and releases the writer lease. Its store is a client; edits apply over the engine's own record.

nodes.label: Covers
nodes.rationale: From the files' tags as small JPEGs; missing ones looked up on Deezer, iTunes, MusicBrainz, then Discogs with the user's token. Other devices get covers from GLUE Home, never from GLUE Cloud.

nodes.label: Discogs
nodes.rationale: The collection and wantlist are read by GLUE Home into discogs.json and matched to songs on the page; Discogs playlists mix songs and vinyl tracks, kept under Discogs.

nodes.label: Gluey (tours and help)
nodes.rationale: Tours are data pointing at data-guide parts of the UI; the first tour shows once per person, with seen kept across the browser, the GLUE folder and the account. A feature's change updates its help article and tour.

nodes.label: Caches
nodes.rationale: Not in the GLUE folder: the browser's OPFS cache kept per collection, and GLUE Home's cache. GLUE Home tidies its cache daily; the files of songs no longer in their collection go after two days' grace.

nodes.label: GLUE Home's first run
nodes.rationale: A guide at the top of its window (account, GLUE folder, incoming folder, start with the computer) until finished or hidden; its window opens on the library, signed in by GLUE Home.

nodes.label: Opening shows its progress
nodes.rationale: Opening the library shows a card with a bar and a top line while the collection is read.

nodes.label: Look (themes and Hallmark)
nodes.rationale: The theme table generates every theme's tokens and shared surfaces; Hallmark's Console treatment with sentence-case labels, measured mono and no emoji.

nodes.label: Downloads
nodes.rationale: Songs saved as files; ranges from GLUE Home so a dropped connection resumes; a zip written as it goes.
